raw_response:
I farm only 4.5 mu, and with just two people at home I will not spread myself too thin. I will keep the main money on cabbage and eggplant, because that cabbage-eggplant rotation is what I know best, and on my side of Hebei it fits the season and water from the well. I usually start from what I did last year, then move a little. If a crop gave steady yield, I do not change much. If neighbors got better stand or better price with a hybrid, I will follow that, but I still watch cost. On small land, every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but losing yield costs more, so on cabbage, cauliflower, chili, and eggplant I will feed a bit heavier and split topdressing after the plants get going. Spinach and kidney bean I will keep lighter, because they do not need the same push. I will plough the heavier plots once before planting, then use rotary tillage where the ground is already loose enough. With well irrigation, I will not wait for the sky; I will water after transplanting, then hold moisture steady, especially for cabbage heading and eggplant, chili, and bean fruiting. Pesticide I will not spray by calendar only, but in a normal year I know roughly how many times each crop usually needs around here, so I budget that in from the start.
